If a dispute arises under this policy, the parties have 30 days to agree on a single arbitrator before the dispute is referred to a panel of three arbitrators.

Here's what you need to know:

- If a dispute arises, the parties must agree on a single arbitrator within 30 days.
- If they cannot agree on a single arbitrator within 30 days, the dispute will be referred to a panel of three arbitrators.
- The panel of three arbitrators will consist of two arbitrators, one appointed by each party, and a third arbitrator appointed by the two arbitrators who will act as the presiding arbitrator.
- The arbitration will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996.

Bottom line: If a dispute arises under this policy, the parties have 30 days to agree on a single arbitrator, or the dispute will be referred to a panel of three arbitrators.

For beta, gamma, and low toxicity alpha emitters, the maximum permissible level is 4 Becquerels/cm2, which is equivalent to 10^-4 microcuries/cm2. For all other emitters, the maximum permissible level is 0.4 Becquerels/cm2.

Bottom line: The policy covers aircraft with radioactive contamination levels up to 4 Becquerels/cm2 for certain types of emitters and 0.4 Becquerels/cm2 for all other emitters.
